research_scope: Five full mathematics reviews, ten unassigned classifications and two mistaken prior subset links corrected, no new meanings or sources.

amendments.review_rationale: Read Cartesian product of S and T as set of all ordered pairs with first coordinate from S and second from T, retaining ordered nature.
amendments.reason: Reviewed whole mathematical formulation and complete dependency adjacency; separated defining axioms from external prerequisites and corrected incorrect subset links.

references.disposition: Set-builder membership constraints characterize product elements; a subset relation between sets is not being asserted.

references.matching_note: Ordered pair is a reusable positional pair, with Kuratowski a possible set model.

references.disposition: The set of all such ordered pairs is the Cartesian product being defined, so self-linking would be circular.
Product S×T is not identical by literal equality to T×S in general.

amendments.review_rationale: Read mapping f:X→Y as total single-valued assignment from every domain input x to exactly one output y∈Y, retaining typed codomain.
amendments.reason: Reviewed whole mathematical formulation and complete dependency adjacency; separated defining axioms from external prerequisites and corrected incorrect subset links.

references.disposition: X and Y are arbitrarily supplied domain and codomain sets, not an instance of a subset relation.

references.phrase: totality for all x in X
references.disposition: Coverage of every x in the domain is an explicit defining axiom of the total function.
Existence of exactly one output is the defining single-valuedness condition.

references.phrase: function need not be injective or surjective
references.disposition: Single-valued total assignment allows repeated outputs and unused codomain elements.

amendments.review_rationale: Reviewed the complete non-strict subset relation between sets by the universal membership implication, explicitly allowing equality and avoiding the stronger proper-subset interpretation.
amendments.reason: Reviewed whole mathematical formulation and complete dependency adjacency; separated defining axioms from external prerequisites and corrected incorrect subset links.

references.phrase: element membership x in A and B
references.disposition: Element membership is foundational and appears inside the defining subset predicate, not as another inclusion meaning.
The quantified membership implication is the defining predicate of non-strict subset.
The condition A subseteq B is non-strict and remains true for A=B; no properness requirement is part of this definition.

amendments.review_rationale: Read proper-subset definition with both non-strict inclusion and strict inequality; the extra witness of an element in B outside A is required, not optional.
amendments.reason: Reviewed whole mathematical formulation and complete dependency adjacency; separated defining axioms from external prerequisites and corrected incorrect subset links.

references.phrase: strict inequality A not equal B
references.disposition: Set inequality distinguishes strict from non-strict inclusion as part of the definition.

references.phrase: element of B not in A
references.disposition: Existence of an element of B outside A is the equivalent defining witness for properness.
Unlike the ordinary subset relation, A and B cannot be identical under this condition.

amendments.review_rationale: Read monoid as set with internal associative binary operation and two-sided identity, without inverse axioms; distinct from group.
amendments.reason: Reviewed whole mathematical formulation and complete dependency adjacency; separated defining axioms from external prerequisites and corrected incorrect subset links.

references.disposition: Associativity is a defining monoid axiom and not an independent prerequisite of this definition.

references.context: Algebra: identity e of a binary operation ⋆ on M such that e⋆x=x⋆e=x for every x in M.
references.reason: Two-sided identity element is reusable independently in monoids, groups and unital rings.

references.disposition: A monoid need not be a group; all group elements have inverses, monoid elements may not.
